summary: Read-only review complete: 7 findings. No edits, builds, tests, network access, or .env reads.

findings.title: Registration cannot satisfy the mandatory existing-credential lookup
findings.detail: The contract applies to every verification and requires the submitted credential to exist and belong to the session owner, then locks it and checks its fingerprint. A new registration has no such row until step 8, so both registration endpoints reject valid enrolments. Password and mailbox grant confirmation also lack the clientDataJSON required by this universal contract. Existing proof flows distinguish these cases explicitly: packages/api/src/auth/admin-staff.ts:64-113 and packages/api/src/routes/customer-tokens.ts:119-146.
findings.fix: Specify separate registration, assertion, password-proof, mailbox-proof, and grant-consumption branches. Registration must derive ownership from the authenticated session and registration challenge, verify attestation, then insert the previously unknown credential.

findings.title: Pending management authorization survives a password change
findings.detail: Only credentials carry recovery fingerprints; grants and registration challenges do not. packages/api/src/routes/account.ts:382-393 changes the password while preserving the calling session. An attacker sharing that session can obtain a grant or registration challenge using the old password, wait for the owner's password change and passkey wipe, then register a new credential bound to the new hash. Owner-first serialization does not invalidate the already-issued authorization. The promised registration-versus-password-change test therefore cannot pass as specified.
findings.fix: Bind grants and registration challenges to the recovery state at proof issuance, propagate that binding through grant consumption, and compare it under the owner lock before registration or deletion. Invalidate pending authorization during credential changes, including changes that retain the calling session.

findings.title: Mailbox management tokens have no specified initiating-browser binding
findings.detail: The request sets a nonce cookie, but the token mint stores no nonce or initiating session, and confirmation checks only token kind, customer, and store. packages/api/src/auth/magic-link.ts:53-80 supplies no browser binding. Binding the resulting grant to the confirming browser does not bind the emailed proof to its initiating browser: a copied link can be redeemed from another live session for the customer with that browser's independently obtained nonce. The actual browser-bound precedent stores the nonce hash in authenticated claims and compares it before redemption: packages/api/src/auth/federated-link.ts:76-106 and packages/api/src/routes/auth.ts:411-418.
findings.fix: Persist the initiating session hash and nonce hash in the passkey_manage token payload or a linked pending-proof row. Require exact matches, live session, current eligibility, and verified email under the owner lock before atomically consuming the token and issuing the grant.

findings.title: Storage-format maintenance invalidates legitimate passkeys
findings.detail: The fingerprints identify stored representations rather than recovery events. packages/api/src/routes/auth.ts:170-175 replaces a customer's password hash during an ordinary successful login when its algorithm or work factor needs upgrading. That invalidates every existing customer passkey without a password change. Likewise, packages/api/src/auth/totp-secret.ts:58-88 seals or unseals an unchanged TOTP secret, changing the proposed admin fingerprint; sealing is invoked during startup at packages/api/src/sdk/create-app.ts:313. These paths contradict the promise that unaffected credentials survive maintenance and rollback.
findings.fix: Define representation-preserving transitions explicitly. Atomically rebind only still-valid customer credentials during verified password rehash, and use a stable protected fingerprint of the logical TOTP secret or an equivalent version scheme. Address previous-image rehash behavior and add unchanged-password and unchanged-TOTP maintenance controls.

findings.title: The existing password-change path still acquires session before owner
findings.detail: packages/api/src/routes/account.ts:382-388 calls me/resolveCustomer before updating the customer. For renewable sessions near expiry, packages/api/src/auth/session.ts:147-151 first updates and locks the session. A concurrent passkey verification following this design holds the customer and waits for that session, while password change holds the session and waits for the customer. Adding the proposed passkey wipe does not remove this deadlock. The document's owner-first claim and no-deadlock acceptance criteria omit this existing writer.
findings.fix: Include signed-in password changes in the lock-order changes. Perform identification in a completed transaction, then lock the customer before any session renewal or locking, revalidate credential proof and session, and perform password replacement, passkey invalidation, and session revocation together. Specify a renewable-session concurrency control.

findings.title: Negative-only login matrix cells do not prove public admission
findings.detail: Eight invalid-assertion 401 cells plus an anonymous success control cannot prove that valid assertions work when unrelated agent, service, stale, or foreign credentials are supplied. An erroneous credential gate can reject those callers while all planned controls still pass. This differs from the existing login model: packages/api/src/sdk/authorization-matrix.identity-cases.testkit.ts:221-232 supplies genuine body credentials and proves successful session creation for every principal. Its shared helper also interprets 401 as NOT_AUTHENTICATED at line 96, which is not ceremony-failure evidence.
findings.fix: Use a fresh valid assertion and browser-bound challenge for each public-login principal cell, proving that the assertion selects the account and creates exactly one session. Keep invalid-assertion cases as supplemental controls and add stale-cookie and enrolment-only-cookie success controls.

findings.title: Agent-policy registration and disabled-feature inventories are missing
findings.detail: Delivery lists allowlist, CSRF, and PUBLIC changes but omits auth/agent-policy.ts. Engine routes absent from its explicit deny map fall through (packages/api/src/auth/agent-policy.ts:86-99), and GET routes bypass that map entirely, so session admission alone does not implement the promised HUMAN outcomes. The static gate also requires every DELETE and every /verify or /step-up mutation to be denied or explicitly excepted (packages/api/scripts/assert-agent-boundary.mjs:12-21). Public passkey login/verify needs an exception. Conversely, unconditional new deny/exception entries fail that same gate when PASSKEYS_ENABLED=0 removes their routes.
findings.fix: Specify requireHuman on authenticated admin passkey routes, the exact management deny entries, and the public login-verification exception. Make route and policy inventories agree in both flag states, and qualify enabled and disabled configurations explicitly.
